proposals.evidence: Turner dhūma explicitly gives Awan/Punjabi dhūā̃, Hindi/Nepali dhuwā̃ and western Pahari dhũ/dhuwā̃ smoke. The western t-initial forms reflect the established local devoicing of old voiced aspirates, while the Maiya/Kullui forms retain their local vowel, nasal and h placement. This comparison is to the smoke noun, not the separate dhūmikā feminine branch.
